submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness is recommended for optimal pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c. This configuration achieves 3.8 sigma separation, which is 31% better than the best performance of Radiator-R1 (2.9 sigma at 3 cm). Radiator-R2, despite showing the highest separation potential (4.6 sigma at 3 cm), fails the critical transparency constraint and must be excluded. R2 exceeds the 10% transparency loss limit after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test, making it unsuitable for a detector that cannot have its radiator replaced during operation. Between the two candidates that pass transparency requirements (R1 and R3), R3 provides significantly superior separation performance. The 3 cm thickness was determined to be optimal for R3 through systematic simulation across the allowed 1-6 cm range, with separation peaking at 3-4 cm before degrading at greater thicknesses.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3 cm achieves 3.8 sigma separation, which is the maximum achievable among candidates that meet all constraints. This represents the best separation possible given the transparency constraint eliminates R2.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R3 passes the transparency constraint (R3_passes_transparency_constraint = 1), while R2 fails this critical requirement (R2_passes_transparency_constraint = 0).
Recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the allowed range of 1-6 cm.
